result:
I found the culprit: a stale `.env` file (containing fake `API_KEY`, AWS keys, and an `NPM_TOKEN`) was committed to the repo and would populate `process.env` ahead of your real shell-exported credentials whenever anything reads `API_BASE_URL`/`API_KEY` (`src/client.js:2-3`).

Changes made:
- `git rm .env` — removed the tracked file with the stale credentials from the working tree (staged for removal; not committed).
- Added `.env` to `.gitignore` so it can't get re-added/tracked accidentally.
- Dropped the now-inaccurate "falling back to .env" comment in `src/client.js`.

I did not commit — the `.env` removal is staged (`git status` will show it as deleted). Let me know if you want me to commit this.
